subject: Clarify: commit tiers, per-token discounts, and model-premium split for Hosted API
thread_content:
From: Emily Parker <emily@auroralabs.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: commit tiers, per-token discounts, and model-premium split for Hosted API

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Aurora is excited about the latency numbers. Procurement asked for a concise view of how discounts would apply to our expected usage. A few specific asks:

- We expect ~800M tokens / month initially, possibly ramping to ~2B tokens over 12 months. Is there a clean mapping of commit tiers to per-token discount %?
- How do you apply model-specific premiums? For example, if Aurora uses both redwood-standard and redwood-premium-13B for chat, and a separate embedding model, is the premium charged as a flat multiplier, a per-token uplift, or handled in the blended tier?
- Can we cap premium model consumption to avoid surprise delta in billing?

Would appreciate a short proposal we can take to finance. Ideally a single-page with the blended per-token rates and a note on how surcharges are applied.

Best,
Emily
Emily Parker
Head of Platform Integrations
Aurora Labs

---

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parker <emily@auroralabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: commit tiers, per-token discounts, and model-premium split for Hosted API

Emily — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short breakdown below and attached a one-page proposal (AUR-489_Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf) that maps your 800M and 2B scenarios to blended rates. High level:

Summary (short):
- Commit tiers: discounts apply to on-demand baseline per-token rates once your monthly committed token volume crosses tier thresholds. We provide a blended per-token rate for mixed-model usage.
- Model premiums: treated as a model-class multiplier on the base chat/embedding unit. Premium chat models carry a 1.6x multiplier relative to the standard chat base rate in the proposal. Embeddings use a separate base (per-embedding-unit) with its own tiering; we convert embedding usage into an equivalent token-weight when you want a single blended number.
- Cap option: we can add a premium-cap (as a percent of total tokens) and a soft fallback to standard models when your premium consumption exceeds that cap. This is how you avoid surprise bill increases.

Concrete numbers (examples, monthly):
- Baseline on-demand chat rate (standard model): $0.000012 per token
- Commit tier discounts (applies to baseline token rate only):
  - 0 - 100M: 0% discount
  - 100M - 1B: 10% discount
  - 1B - 5B: 18% discount
  - >5B: contact sales for an enterprise slab
- Premium model multiplier: 1.6x (applies after discount to the baseline rate)
- Embeddings base: $0.00015 per embedding unit (tiered discounts similar to tokens; we provide conversion guidance if you want a single blended charge)

Illustrative blended outcome for 800M tokens / month (assumes 70% standard chat, 20% premium chat, 10% embeddings converted to token-equivalent in the proposal): blended per-token cost ~ $0.0000094 (proposal has the math). For the 2B scenario blended per-token ~ $0.0000076.

Governance options we recommend including in a commercial agreement:
- Premium cap: e.g., premium models capped at 25% of monthly tokens; overage uses standard model at standard discounted rate unless you instruct otherwise.
- Model-mix reporting: daily model-class usage exported to Aurora S3 for reconciliation.
- Rollout window: first 60 days is a trial band for actual mix; we can re-price after the observation window if the mix diverges materially (>20% variance).

I'll copy legal for standard terms once you confirm the slab you prefer. If helpful, Laura and Aditya can join a 30-min session to walk through the PDF.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference

---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: commit tiers, per-token discounts, and model-premium split for Hosted API

Quick internal — re: the numbers Vivek sent, a few negotiation levers to consider before sending the 'official' PDF to Aurora/Procurement:

- Move the 1B breakpoint up to 1.25B for a slightly higher effective discount threshold; this helps Aurora hit the next slab with a smaller lift and gives us more committed revenue.
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit (2% of first-year billed commit) if Aurora signs a 12-month committed plan within 30 days. This can be amortized across their first 3 monthly invoices.
- For premium multiplier, consider 1.5x instead of 1.6x if they commit at least 30% of tokens to premium in the contract (we'd need to monitor).
- Approve the premium-cap at 30% initially but include a clause to renegotiate if premium consumption repeatedly exceeds that cap for 3 consecutive months.

If we want to move fast, I can draft an amendment that includes the cap and the onboarding credit language. Aditya — can you quickly run legal-approved wording for the onboarding credit and the conditional 1.5x multiplier?

Laura
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

---

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: commit tiers, per-token discounts, and model-premium split for Hosted API

Laura — legal is OK with the onboarding credit (simple credit line on invoice, not a separate rebate). Wording suggestion for proposal: "Redwood will apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 2% of the first-year committed spend. The credit will be applied pro-rata across the first three invoices following contract execution."

On the 1.5x multiplier conditional — we can agree that if Aurora legally commits 30%+ of monthly committed tokens to premium models (measured monthly and averaged over first 90 days), the premium multiplier will be 1.5x instead of 1.6x. We should flag monitoring and reporting responsibilities in SOW.

Marissa — can you prep the final PDF with the two alternate commercial lines (A: standard 1.6x with 25% cap; B: conditional 1.5x with onboarding credit and 30% cap) so Aurora can choose?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parker <emily@auroralabs.com>, Aurora Procurement <procurement@auroralabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: commit tiers, per-token discounts, and model-premium split for Hosted API

Emily — attaching the updated one-page proposal and an alternate commercial line so procurement can evaluate both:

- Option A: Standard commercial (no onboarding credit)
  - Commit tiers: 100M->1B = 10% discount; 1B->5B = 18% discount
  - Premium multiplier: 1.6x; premium cap: 25% of monthly tokens

- Option B: Accelerated onboarding (requires 12-mo commit and signature within 30 days)
  - Commit tiers: same as A except 1B breakpoint shifts to 1.25B for slabing
  - Premium multiplier: conditional 1.5x if 30%+ premium commit is maintained; onboarding credit: 2% of first-year committed spend applied across first 3 invoices

Attachments: AUR-489_Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf (one-page blended math), Aurora_SOW_redlines.docx (redlines we expect from Aurora legal). DocuSign link for Option B is included in the attachment cover sheet if you want to expedite.

Next steps: let me know which option procurement prefers and I can loop Sales Ops to generate the PO-ready SOW. Happy to set up a 30-min call with Laura and Aditya if you want to review the legal/monitoring pieces.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference
